clue.text: Return game in Japan needs support

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game of black and white stones
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A rematch of some game played in Japan needs backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back somewhere is to return there; the phrasal verb is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Boy admitting mislaying alphabetical list

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name
mislaying something means its loss

explanation.surface: A boy confesses to losing a list of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of terms with explanations, usually in alphabetical order at the back of a book.

clue.text: Before flying etc abroad, one should get ecclesiastical approval

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Advice to get a priest's blessing before taking a flight overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'abroad' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefit of clergy is the rites or sanction of the church, as in marriage 'without benefit of clergy'.

clue.text: Symptom of fear beginning to concern old soldier

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word
taken as written
an old sweat is British slang for a veteran soldier

explanation.surface: An old soldier starts to show signs of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldier' seems one unit, the slang 'old sweat'; here 'old' is taken literally and the soldier gives SWEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sweat is perspiration with chills, a bodily reaction to fright.

clue.text: A noisy business house editor swore

parts.note: taken as written
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a firm is a business house
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor at a rowdy company let fly with a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swore' looks like cursing, but here it means declared on oath.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state solemnly, so 'affirmed' is a past-tense synonym of swore in its oath-taking sense.

clue.text: A series of transparencies records journey

parts.note: to film is to record on camera
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A holiday slide show documents a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A filmstrip is a length of film carrying a sequence of still images for projection, like slides.

clue.text: One with hand that's perfect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a deal is the hand of cards dealt to a player

explanation.surface: A card player holding a flawless hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect, the best that could be imagined.

clue.text: Film — The Witching Hour, say

parts.note: the witching hour is midnight, when witches are said to be abroad
to express is to say

explanation.surface: Naming a film called The Witching Hour, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' after a title, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Express is the 1978 Alan Parker film about an American jailed in Turkey.

clue.text: County Durham's first store, refurbished

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

indicators.note: something refurbished is done up and rearranged, so the letters change order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: County Durham's first shop has been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County Durham' reads as one name, but 'County' is the definition and Durham only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on the south coast of England.

clue.text: A mostly gloomy (according to some Americans) Indian city

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
gray is the American spelling of grey, dull and gloomy

explanation.surface: An Indian city that some American visitors found rather dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh, India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Have in one's possession some half-crowns

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only a part of the following word, a run of its letters

parts.note: three consecutive letters sit inside the second word of the compound

explanation.surface: Someone owns a few old half-crown coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-crown was a pre-decimal British coin worth two shillings and sixpence; the next clue picks up on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it as your property, the plain verb sense.

clue.text: … no longer this — tell grandee differently

indicators.note: doing something differently means rearranging it, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: Someone must break it to a nobleman that his old coins are worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue: half-crowns stopped being valid money in 1970, so the definition is completed by that clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency that must be accepted in payment, which withdrawn coins such as half-crowns no longer are.

clue.text: Flatters light kitchen-sink dramas?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sweet-talks, coaxes with flattery
second meaning, read as two words: gentle television serials about domestic life

explanation.walkthrough: A soap is a TV serial, and kitchen-sink drama is gritty domestic realism; making it 'light' gives soft soaps. The question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap someone is an idiom for persuading them with flattery.

clue.text: River, one featured in superstitions

indicators.note: something featured in a thing appears inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional beliefs, including superstitions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A river that figures in local superstition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Poor, born round unpleasant old constituency

parts.note: rotten means of poor quality
b. is the abbreviation for born in dates
O is round in shape
a rough time is an unpleasant one

explanation.surface: A description of someone born poor and surrounded by nastiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a container signal around 'unpleasant', but it simply gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten borough was a pre-1832 British parliamentary seat with very few voters, controlled by a patron.

clue.text: Singers in pub (Italian one) on Sunday

parts.note: a bar is a pub
It. is the abbreviation for Italian
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Singers performing in a pub, one of them Italian, on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Baritones are male singers whose range lies between tenor and bass.

clue.text: United Nations told it's beside the point

parts.note: UN is the abbreviation for United Nations
to relate a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: The United Nations were told the issue was irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrelated has no connection to the matter in hand, so it is irrelevant.

clue.text: Resign from favourite Society, upset and depressed

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
S is the abbreviation for society
feeling down means depressed

explanation.surface: A favourite member quits a society, upset and low.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is an idiom for resigning from a post.

clue.text: Tense time ahead? Correct

parts.note: the future is the time yet to come
perfect means without error, correct

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about what lies ahead is asked whether that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, but it is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The future perfect ('will have done') is a verb tense in grammar.

clue.text: Submarines about at sea, heading for Suez

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Submarines patrolling the sea on their way to the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German military submarines of the two World Wars.

clue.text: What a gaucho may have imported into Maracaibo — lasso?

indicators.note: something imported into a place is carried inside it, so the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the city name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a South American cowboy's lasso was shipped into the Venezuelan port of Maracaibo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolas are throwing weapons of weighted cords used by gauchos, the cowboys of the pampas, to catch animals.

clue.text: Undisturbed, yet subdued
Unduly led astray by Philip for so long

parts.note: unduly means excessively, too

indicators.note: led astray means taken off course, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
Pip is a pet form of Philip, as in Great Expectations

explanation.surface: Someone was badly misled by a man named Philip for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a measure of time but it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is old-fashioned British slang for goodbye, just as 'so long' is.

clue.text: Ring writer ready to entertain new ideas

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer phones, willing to hear fresh suggestions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is the shape of the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be open to ideas is to be receptive and willing to consider them.

clue.text: This legal process involved errant gamin

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the fodder; a gamin is a street urchin

explanation.surface: A court procedure brought against a wayward street child.
explanation.definitionFit: An arraignment is the formal reading of charges to an accused in court, a step in criminal procedure.

clue.text: One's image of oneself, for example, facing Opposition's leader

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A politician's self-image set against the Opposition leader's, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is a person's sense of self-esteem and self-importance.

clue.text: Small telescope used by agent, good young woman

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
G is the abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A secret agent and a well-behaved girl share a pocket telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, as once carried by sailors.

clue.text: One worried about onset of debility is an inventor

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others
something worried is agitated or shaken about, so its letters move

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so take the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about growing frail turns out to be an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged 'one' wraps around D and the word 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.
